scenes.title: HURRICANE SIMON
vo: This hurricane was so strong, it sent ripples through the sky high above its own clouds.
Here's how a storm gets that powerful.

scenes.title: LEVEL 1
vo: It starts over warm ocean water near the equator.
Warm, wet air rises off the surface.

scenes.title: LEVEL 2
vo: Rising air leaves low pressure, so more air rushes in and rises too.
Its water turns into towering clouds.

scenes.title: LEVEL 3
vo: Earth's rotation twists the incoming air into a counterclockwise spin.
At seventy-four miles per hour, it's a hurricane, with a calm eye in the middle.

scenes.title: LEVEL 4
vo: Simon hit about two hundred fifty kilometers per hour off Mexico's Pacific coast.
Its eye passed just fifty kilometers from shore.

scenes.title: BONUS
vo: At night, a satellite saw ripples spreading from the storm, glowing high in the atmosphere.
Gravity waves, pushed up by its huge updrafts.
